subject: mechanical
audience: FE Mechanical candidates and mechanical engineering students
title: The 30 kW Shaft That Needed 239 N·m of Torque
featured_title: THE 30 KW SHAFT THAT NEEDED 239 N M OF TORQUE

presentation.challenge: The shaft power was 30 kW at 1200 rpm. That meant about 239 N·m torque, not 30 N·m.

practice.primary_question: How are shaft power, rotational speed, and torque related in mechanical power transmission?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Treating power in kilowatts as if it were numerically equal to torque in newton-meters.

case_dna.target_misconception: A 30 kW shaft can be assumed to carry 30 N·m torque because the numerical power value is 30.
case_dna.why_plausible: Power and torque are both common shaft ratings, and unit conversion between rpm and rad/s is easy to skip.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: P=Tω and ω=2πN/60. At 30 kW and 1200 rpm, ω≈125.66 rad/s and T≈238.7 N·m.
case_dna.corrected_model: Rotating mechanical power is P=Tω, so torque depends on both power and shaft speed.

problem_statement: A drive shaft transmits 30 kW at 1200 rpm. A component-selection note assumes 30 N·m torque because the power rating is 30 kW. Calculate the actual transmitted torque and determine what happens to torque if the same power is transmitted at 600 rpm.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The power rating was 30 kW. The torque was nearly eight times 30 N·m.
gates.prompt: What conversion is required before solving for torque?

options.label: Use P=Tω with ω=2πN/60
options.reason: Rotating power is torque times angular velocity.

options.label: Set torque equal to the numerical kW value
options.reason: Power and torque have different units and depend on speed.

options.label: Use P=TN directly with N in rpm
options.reason: RPM must be converted to angular speed or used with an equivalent conversion formula.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict transmitted torque
gates.prompt: What torque in N·m corresponds to 30 kW at 1200 rpm?

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Measure shaft torque
gates.result: The shaft torque is about 239 N·m.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the torque
gates.prompt: Use T=P/ω with P=30,000 W and ω=2π(1200)/60. Enter N·m.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Speed determines how much torque is needed for a given power

cards.text: At constant power, lower rotational speed requires higher torque.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the shaft-rating note
report: C2. The shaft rotates at 1200 rpm.
C3. Therefore shaft torque is 30 N·m.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: It equates unlike units and ignores rotational speed.

evidence_choices.label: T=30,000/[2π(1200)/60]≈238.7 N·m
evidence_choices.reason: This is the correct power-speed-torque relation.

correction.template: The transmitted torque is about {torque} N·m at 1200 rpm.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Transmit the same 30 kW at 600 rpm

options.label: Torque doubles to about 477.5 N·m
options.reason: At constant power, halving angular speed doubles torque.

options.label: Torque halves to about 119.4 N·m
options.reason: Lower speed requires more torque at the same power.

options.label: Torque stays 238.7 N·m
options.reason: Torque depends inversely on angular speed for fixed power.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply power-speed scaling
gates.prompt: For fixed power, what happens to torque if shaft speed doubles?

options.label: Torque doubles
options.reason: Torque is inversely proportional to speed at fixed power.

gates.explanation: For a fixed power requirement, torque varies inversely with angular speed.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the power-transmission calculation
gates.confirmation: I confirm that shaft torque must be calculated from both transmitted power and rotational speed.

items.label: What failed
items.value: The numerical power rating was mistaken for a torque value.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: Power equals torque times angular speed.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use P=Tω with consistent SI units.

seo.seo_title: Shaft Power, Speed and Torque: 30 kW at 1200 rpm | FE E-060
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Mechanical Case E-060: a shaft transmitting 30 kW at 1200 rpm carries about 239 N·m torque.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE Mechanical shaft power torque speed
seo.excerpt: Power does not determine shaft torque by itself. Rotational speed is the second part of the equation.
seo.direct_answer: Rotating mechanical power is P=Tω. At 30 kW and 1200 rpm, ω=2πN/60≈125.66 rad/s, so T≈30,000/125.66=238.7 N·m. At the same power and 600 rpm, torque doubles.

faqs.q: How do you calculate torque from power and rpm?
faqs.a: Convert rpm to angular speed with ω=2πN/60, then use T=P/ω.

faqs.q: What happens to torque if speed is halved at constant power?
